trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going left would strand number 2: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going left, the next 13 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,3). So the line goes down.
Cell (2,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going up, the next 12 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2); going down, the next 10 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,3). So the line goes left.

Going to number 3 would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (1,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (3,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going right would leave both cell (4,6) and number 5 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would force the line onto number 5 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going up would leave both cell (4,3) and cell (4,5) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
The line must go right: left is number 9, which comes later.
Going up would leave both cell (3,1) and cell (3,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Cell (3,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (5,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
